Quoting & estimating tools for Electricians

Tools that help electricians with quoting & estimating. Producing estimates and bids faster — measuring, takeoffs, material pricing and proposal writing.

Where Quoting & estimating goes wrong for Electricians

Electrical estimating has to account for circuit counts, cable runs and certification work, which is hard to price from memory. Under-quoting a rewire is one of the most expensive mistakes in the trade.

What Electricians jobs really involve

Electrical work carries certification and documentation duties that most other trades do not, so paperwork is genuinely part of the job rather than an optional extra. Records of what was installed and tested matter long after the invoice is paid.

Frequently asked questions

Which quoting & estimating tools work best for electricians?

The three that fit best here are Joist (Solo contractors and small crews who mainly need to quote and get paid), Knowify (Contractors who need to know whether a job actually made money), Jobber (Owner-operators and small crews moving off paper and spreadsheets). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does quoting & estimating software cost for electricians?

Across the 6 tools on this page, 4 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does quoting & estimating cause problems for electricians specifically?

Electrical estimating has to account for circuit counts, cable runs and certification work, which is hard to price from memory. Under-quoting a rewire is one of the most expensive mistakes in the trade.

Do I need software that stores electrical certificates?

Any system that lets you attach test results and certificates to a job and find them again later is enough. Dedicated certification apps only start to matter when you are issuing a large number of certificates every month.
